Camera, tracking & help
At a desk, keep your shoulders in the picture to see your collarbones, shoulder blades, ribs and spine; they no longer need your hips to be visible. For a full-body view, step back until your hips and feet are visible, with even lighting. Keep your hand closer to the camera to see its detailed bones; farther away, simpler hand bones and a stand-in skull follow the body tracker. If movement looks slow, switch Body tracking to Fast and reload. Use Space to freeze or resume and S to save an image when you’re not typing.
Camera access starts only after the models are loaded. The browser restricts network requests for that session. The tracking and anatomy models are downloaded from Google and a CDN; those services can see the download request and IP address. Camera frames are processed locally.
Anatomy models: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science, CC BY-SA 2.1 Japan. Head and hand meshes simplified and realigned in the original mirror; body bones adapted from the OrganUI skeleton. Three.js (MIT) and MediaPipe Tasks (Apache 2.0) code is included in this file. Body overlays are approximate and may not match your joints.
